title: Add slugify to textutil
prompt:
Add a function `slugify(text, max_length=None)` to `textutil.py`. The module already has two unrelated helpers, `word_count` and `title_case`; leave them working exactly as they are.

Visible tests (a partial set; the slugify ones currently fail): `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`

Specification:
1. `text` must be a `str`; anything else (None, int, bytes, ...) raises `TypeError`.
2. `max_length` is `None` (no limit) or an integer; `max_length < 1` raises `ValueError`. Both checks happen up front, before any other processing, even when the text is empty or already short; the type of `text` is checked first.
3. Normalise `text` with Unicode NFKD, then remove every character that is not ASCII. Accents and other combining marks come off; characters with no ASCII decomposition (for example `ß`, `æ`, CJK) are simply deleted: deleted, not replaced by a separator, and there is no transliteration table.
4. Lower-case the result.
5. Every run of one or more characters outside `[a-z0-9]` becomes a single `-`.
6. Strip leading and trailing `-`.
7. If nothing is left, the result is exactly `"n-a"` (returned as is; `max_length` does not apply to it).
8. If `max_length` is given and the slug is longer than it, shorten it to at most `max_length` characters: when the cut falls inside a word, cut back to the previous `-` boundary and drop the partial word; if the first word alone is longer than `max_length`, hard-cut it at `max_length` characters. The result never ends with `-`. A slug that already fits is returned unchanged.

Examples:
    slugify("Hello, World!")            == "hello-world"
    slugify("Crème Brûlée")             == "creme-brulee"
    slugify("hello big world", 12)      == "hello-big"    # 'hello-big-wo' cuts inside 'world'
    slugify("hello big world", 6)       == "hello"        # 'hello-' would end with '-'
    slugify("hello big world", 5)       == "hello"
    slugify("supercalifragilistic", 5)  == "super"
    slugify("日本語")                    == "n-a"
